title: Ringed geometric-point evaluation with signed tensor and coefficient models
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and use the small pro-etale site and geometric stalk of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. For a sheaf of commutative rings $B$ on this site put $R=B(s)$. The topos point associated to $\operatorname{id}_s$ has inverse image canonically identified with final-object sections, by the restriction maps $\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal F(s)$ along pointed lifts $s\to U$. With the identity ring map to $R$, its module pullback is canonically $\Gamma_s=\Gamma(s,-)$, and its total derived pullback is the functor induced by termwise exact sections [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact].
For K-flat complexes $P,Q$ of $B$-modules with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], there is a natural chain isomorphism
$$ b_{P,Q}:\Gamma_s\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_B Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}(\Gamma_sP\otimes_R\Gamma_sQ). $$
Its inverse sends $x\otimes y$ to the section tensor of $x,y$. The image complexes are K-flat with flat terms. After localization this is precisely the canonical ringed-topos derived pullback comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], identified through exact sections, including its representative comparison maps. This identification is natural in both derived variables and independent of the K-flat models.
The unit comparison is $\Gamma_s B=R$. The maps $b$ intertwine the signed total-complex associators, both unitors and braiding: in degrees $i,j$ the braiding is $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{ij}y\otimes x$, the associator preserves the order of the three generators, and the unitors are multiplication. These are equalities of the specified chain maps and descend to their derived maps. For a morphism $B\to B'$ of commutative ring sheaves, putting $R'=B'(s)$, the square between these tensor comparisons and the canonical derived scalar comparisons commutes. On flat-term models its inverse form is the balanced rule $(x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes b)\mapsto(x\otimes y)\otimes ab$; the squares include identity and composed scalar maps.
For the coefficient sheaves of [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], this identifies $\Gamma_s(A_{E,n})_s=A_{E,n}$ and $\Gamma_s\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}=\mathcal O_E$ with the specified constant-section and quotient maps. The integral assertion here concerns the ordinary ambient tensor, before completion.

proof.text: The pointed final neighbourhood is terminal in the opposite index: the arrow from it to a pointed neighbourhood is its lift. Construct the restriction cocone and its colimit isomorphism, and use naturality of restriction to identify the specified geometric stalk. Equip the recorded geometric morphism with the actual section ring and module evaluation. The underlying operation graphs show that these identifications preserve the ring and module operations.

Evaluation at the final object preserves sheafification, because every covering sieve there contains the identity. Thus evaluation of the sheaf tensor is canonically the tensor of the evaluated modules; its inverse on pure tensors is exactly the recorded section tensor. Compose the lax monoidal forgetful functor with presheaf evaluation. Its binary and unit maps are isomorphisms, so this gives a strong monoidal evaluation functor with the specified module comparisons.

The point description gives preservation of small colimits. Apply the standard mapHomologicalComplex monoidal construction to evaluation; its inverse comparison has the prescribed formula on every total summand. The oplax monoidal equations give naturality, associativity and both unitors. Test the module braiding on pure tensors, then the chain braiding on total summands: additivity preserves the common Koszul sign. Its unit is the single-complex lift of the actual identity on the section ring.

The ringed-site stalk criterion and preservation of flatness imply that evaluation sends the recorded resolving class to flat-term K-flat module complexes. Exactness is the recorded point sections theorem. Existence of flat-term K-flat resolutions makes restriction to resolving representatives fully faithful in the homotopy localization. Apply tensorComparisonDescent with the explicitly constructed chain comparison; left-derived uniqueness identifies the exact descended section functor with every specified left-derived presentation.

Evaluation of scalar extension is identified with ordinary extension of section scalars by the final-object sheafification isomorphism. The identification sends the specified extension pure tensor to its ordinary tensor. The ordinary strong monoidal extension-of-scalars functor supplies the chain scalar comparison and its balanced formula. The module insertion-tensor equation proves the module square on generators; coproduct extensionality and the total-summand comparison formulas lift it to the required chain square.

Ringed-topos pullback along the identity topos preserves the flat-term K-flat class for any coefficient map; ordinary extension of scalars does likewise by base change. Restriction to resolving representatives is fully faithful after localization. Lift the composite of the prescribed representative isomorphisms across this restriction to construct the scalar derived comparison. Cancelling the representative isomorphisms proves its normalization and uniqueness.

Every constant-section map, without a finiteness hypothesis on the ring, is bijective: its sheafification unit is locally bijective and every cover of the final point contains the identity. Naturality of sheafification identifies the residue transition maps, while the limit-lift equation identifies all projections of the integral constant map. The profinite tower isomorphism with the actual quotient maps identifies compatible residues with the integer ring. Evaluation preserves the ring-sheaf limit, so equality on all projections proves bijectivity of the specified integral-section map.

Use the separately stated normalized chain tensor/scalar construction. Combine it with the proved geometric point identification, coefficient quotient/limit calculation and the representative-localization descent arguments in the item module.
